visible_condition.plain_language: A consequential release waits until the operator can see what will cross, why it may cross, and which confirmation makes this exact route lawful.

available_affordances.purpose: Release only the declared packet through the witnessed route and leave an inspectable receipt.

causal_structure.input: declared consequential action plus human confirmation

research_frame.question: Can a consequential security boundary remain child-legible internally while preserving non-equivalent route history and minimum disclosure externally?
research_frame.hypothesis: Consequence-first route disclosure plus explicit human confirmation will reduce operator burden without collapsing route authority into endpoint equivalence.
observable_behavior: operator can state what will cross before confirming
operator can distinguish release from refusal
operator can see that a replayed or alternate path lacks the original route authority
alternative_explanations: shorter wording may improve scanability independently of AIA route structure
prior familiarity with confirmation dialogs may contribute to comprehension
expected_failure_modes: endpoint arrival is treated as authorization
a refusal leaks protected route structure
replay is inferred dead without a durable tombstone
falsifier: operators cannot distinguish endpoint from route authority
an alternate path is accepted solely because it reaches the same endpoint
the system claims durable replay refusal without a persistent spent-intent record
abstention_conditions: the consequential action cannot be represented as a bounded route
human confirmation is unavailable for the protected action
